facts.text: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is the ability of electronics to work correctly amid electrical noise from other equipment without producing noise that disturbs other equipment.
facts.quote: Electromagnetic compatibility is the ability of a piece of electronics to work correctly amid electrical noise from other equipment and to avoid producing noise that disturbs others.

facts.text: Heavy machines present a harsh electrical environment for collision sensors because large motors, inverters, radios and lights share a small space with the sensors' tiny signals.
facts.quote: A machine is a harsh electrical environment, where large motors, inverters, radios and lights share a small space with a collision sensor's tiny signals.

facts.text: ISO 16001, the international standard for object detection systems on earth-moving machines, requires electromagnetic compatibility to ISO 13766.
facts.quote: ISO 16001, the international standard for object detection systems on earth-moving machines, requires EMC to ISO 13766 [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Variable-frequency drives caused nuisance shutdowns of proximity systems in the field.
facts.quote: In the field, variable-frequency drives caused nuisance shutdowns of proximity systems

facts.text: Interference between the zones of different machines was reported in the field.
facts.quote: interference between the zones of different machines was reported

facts.text: Mine leaders reported interference involving personal dust monitors, computers, survey lasers and steel-braided water lines.
facts.quote: mine leaders reported interference involving personal dust monitors, computers, survey lasers and steel-braided water lines [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Queensland guidance asks whether a collision system will interfere with other electronics.
facts.quote: Queensland guidance asks whether a collision system will interfere with other electronics

facts.text: Queensland guidance asks whether a collision system resists deliberate operator interference.
facts.quote: Queensland guidance asks whether a collision system will interfere with other electronics and whether it resists deliberate operator interference [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The booklet identifies electromagnetic compatibility and interference between multiple radars or lidars on one machine or site as a blind spot of sensor simulation.
facts.quote: The booklet lists electromagnetic compatibility and interference between multiple radars or lidars on one machine or site as a blind spot of sensor simulation [Chapter 6].

facts.text: The booklet states that interference does not appear in any simulator and manifests in the field as unexplained nuisance stops or missed detections.
facts.quote: Interference does not appear in any simulator and shows up in the field as unexplained nuisance stops or missed detections

facts.text: Electromagnetic compatibility remains a physical-test item because interference is not represented in simulators.
facts.quote: Interference does not appear in any simulator and shows up in the field as unexplained nuisance stops or missed detections, so EMC remains a physical-test item

facts.text: Collision-system acceptance criteria must account for false triggers caused by electromagnetic interference.
facts.quote: EMC remains a physical-test item and a source of false triggers that the acceptance criteria must account for [Chapters 4, 6].
